posts.title: A journey through the Europe Rome built
posts.description: London did not begin with Londoners. Around the middle of the first century AD, Roman engineers and merchants looked at a stretch of the Thames where the river was narrow enough to bridge and deep enough to take ships, so they decided it was a useful place to build. Londinium grew around that crossing, first as a trading settlement and then as the administrative center of Roman Britain… Source

posts.title: The Ocarina of Budrio: a musical joke that traveled the world
posts.description: Giuseppe Donati was seventeen years old when, in 1853, he made a musical joke for his friends in Budrio, a small town northeast of Bologna. He already knew his way around music: he had studied theory and piano, played clarinet in the local band and organ in church, and what he produced in clay was inspired by the little terracotta whistles sold at fairs, the sort shaped like birds and other… Source

posts.title: Cuccìa: Sicily’s sweet tradition for Saint Lucy’s Day
posts.description: Every December 13, many Sicilian families observe a rather unusual food tradition: they avoid bread and pasta, two foods that would ordinarily be difficult to imagine an Italian table without, and prepare cuccìa, a dish made from whole grains of boiled wheat. The custom is particularly strong in Palermo and Syracuse, where the feast of Santa Lucia has long been associated with the memory of hunger… Source
